Abstract:

Topological insulators provide a unique platform for studying the interplay between topology and&nbspsuperconductivity. In this work, the transport properties of exfoliated BiSbTeSe2 (BSTS) topological&nbspinsulator flakes and amorphous indium oxide (a-InO) films have been investigated. Temperature-dependent measurements on BSTS reveal a crossover from bulk-dominated conduction at high&nbsptemperatures to metallic surface-state transport at low temperatures. Gate-voltage measurements&nbspexhibit a well-defined Dirac point, demonstrating the tunability of the topological surface states. In&nbspcontrast, the a-InO films display strongly insulating behavior characteristic of highly disordered systems&nbspnear the superconductor-insulator transition. At low temperature, the BSTS/a-InO hybrid structure&nbspshowed the superconducting signature even though the InO is in the insulating state. Our results&nbspestablish the fundamental transport properties of the constituent materials and provide a basis for&nbspfuture studies of proximity-induced superconductivity and topological phenomena in BSTS/a-InO&nbsphybrid structures.
